links.outcome: Accuracy of adjuvant therapy recommendations, guideline-grounded RAG vs ungrounded LLMs vs tumor board consensus
links.effect: TSB (Claude-2 + NCCN RAG) accuracy 0.89 vs Claude-2 0.86 (P=.080) and GPT-4 0.78 (P<.001); GPT-4 much lower on genetic testing (OR 0.05).
links.quote: TSB achieved an overall accuracy of 0.89, compared with 0.86 for Claude-2 and 0.78 for GPT-4 across all seven modalities.

links.outcome: Whether AI flagged missing or anomalous input (menopausal status) that prevented valid output
links.effect: In a T2N1 case with unclear menopausal status, TSB recommended Oncotype testing, whereas MTB recommended chemotherapy; AI did not flag the missing variable.
links.quote: The AI did not identify the missing menopausal status as a critical variable.

links.outcome: Concordance of AI treatment recommendations with expert consensus and guidelines, discordant cases
links.effect: TSB recommended endocrine therapy for three low ER-positive DCIS cases where MTB withheld; also recommended redundant genetic testing and RT without considering margin status in two patients.
links.quote: Similarly, TSB automatically recommended RT after lumpectomy in two patients without considering margin status or the need for re-excision.

links.outcome: Accuracy, precision, recall, F1 of AI outputs against MTB consensus reference standard
links.effect: TSB accuracy 0.89, precision 0.85, recall 0.82, F1 0.80; GPT-4 precision 0.60, F1 0.70.
links.quote: The primary outcome was overall performance of the three AI models across seven therapy modalities, using human consensus from MTB as ground truth.

links.outcome: Recommendations reflecting available prior patient data (longitudinal recall)
links.effect: AI recommended genetic testing for a patient who had already undergone testing, reflecting limitation in longitudinal data recall.
links.quote: In another case, the AI recommended GT for a patient who had already undergone testing.

links.outcome: Whether tool displays supporting source content for recommendations
links.effect: TSB output includes a Sources drop-down with guideline excerpts and links; described as improving interpretability, but effect not tested.
links.quote: TSB improves interpretability by referencing relevant clinical guidelines when generating recommendations, thereby enhancing transparency.

links.effect: TSB accuracy 0.89, Claude-2 0.86, and GPT-4 0.78; GPT-4 was significantly lower than TSB (P < .001).
links.quote: TSB achieved an overall accuracy of 0.89, compared with 0.86 for Claude-2 and 0.78 for GPT-4 across all seven modalities.

links.effect: TSB outperformed GPT-4 (estimate –11.2; P < .001), but Claude-2 accuracy reduction versus TSB was nonsignificant (estimate –3.00; P = .080).
links.quote: In the comparative analysis using GEEs, Claude-2 showed a nonsignificant reduction in accuracy compared with TSB (estimate, –3.00 [95% CI, –6.36 to 0.33]; P = .080).

links.effect: Overall accuracy was below 1.0 for all models: TSB 0.89, Claude-2 0.86, GPT-4 0.78.
links.quote: TSB achieved an overall accuracy of 0.89, compared with 0.86 for Claude-2 and 0.78 for GPT-4 across all seven modalities.

links.effect: One discordant Oncotype case had unclear menopausal status; TSB suggested testing while MTB recommended chemotherapy if premenopausal.
links.quote: The AI did not identify the missing menopausal status as a critical variable.

links.effect: One T2N1 case with unclear menopausal status produced an Oncotype Dx recommendation instead of a flagged data gap needing clarification.
